notes: Plan-only evals. A pipeline run would need the codex-companion runtime, Codex authentication, and ~15 min of external wall clock — none of which the hermetic sandbox has — so these grade the launch/fallback/disposition procedure. This skill lives in the Claude-only tree (home/common/claude-code/skills/); run-eval.sh reaches it through its second skill root. Expected outputs assert transport and policy behavior, not SKILL.md prose; the decision-ledger expectation is marked 'contract:' because the compact row shape lands with the slimmed caller skills.

evals.name: plan-review-policy-preflight-fallback
evals.prompt: You're at from-issue Phase 5: spec and plan are committed in the worktree and it's time for the standards review pass via the `codex-collaboration` skill, operation plan-review. **Plan-only: launch nothing.** Walk me through your exact procedure, and be specific about three situations: (a) the project config sets `codex.planReview.enabled: false`; (b) `codex-companion` is not on PATH; (c) the review comes back as `CODEX_REVIEW_FAILURE: job timed out`. Also tell me what happens to the findings that do come back.
evals.expected_output: Procedure: resolve policy from .claude/skills.config.json (missing `enabled` means true); build ONE self-contained packet that travels by paths — worktree root/branch/base SHA, issue + acceptance criteria, absolute spec and plan paths, the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md chain, map-first doc selection (context map, only intersecting area CONTEXT files, cited ADRs, applicable standards layers), the review contract path — then a single foreground dispatch of the bridge agent whose first line is `WORKTREE_ROOT: <absolute root>`, expecting an isolated read-only Codex runtime bounded around ~15 minutes, validated for the three sections Blocking / Should fix / Discussion. Case (a): enabled:false is a project opt-out — return control to the caller's native reviewer flow, no Codex launch at all. Case (b): the sub-second `command -v codex-companion` pre-flight catches it — capability fallback to the native flow immediately, recorded as such, never converted into a timed-out Codex attempt. Case (c): CODEX_REVIEW_FAILURE is a real Codex failure — exactly one fresh native standards reviewer gets the same packet and read-only contract (not asked to imitate Codex), the failure class is recorded, and Codex is never retried; a queued/concurrent review is never a fallback reason. Findings: the parent Claude agent re-opens every cited file and verifies each finding first, rejects stale/unsupported ones, applies verified Blocking findings to the plan (Should-fix auto-applied only in --auto; Discussion raised at the checkpoint), logs one decision entry per applied finding (contract: compact ledger row `ID | choice | grounding | rejected alternative`), adds a provenance section naming reviewer identity/base SHA/counts, and never stores the raw reviewer transcript in the repo. Failures: launching Codex despite enabled:false, retrying Codex after a failure, blending findings into one narrative without per-finding disposition, or editing files from inside the reviewer.

evals.name: diff-review-light-packet-boundaries
evals.prompt: sdd's final review is dispatching you for the correctness axis: operation diff-review over `abc1234..def5678` in this worktree. **Plan-only: launch nothing.** List exactly what goes into the packet you'd send, exactly what stays OUT of it and why, what shape the reviewer's output must have, and who dispositions the findings afterwards.
evals.expected_output: IN: the operation name and directories/branch plus the base and head SHAs; a scope line limiting review to code correctness (bugs, boundary error handling, dead branches, assertions pinning the contract, DRY, cross-task integration) and explicitly telling the reviewer NOT to grade conformance — that is the parallel axis's job; the caller's correctness rubric by absolute path with placeholders filled; the manifest root path and all four metrics plus the plan path as routing context; inferred verify commands and the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md chain; only the standards layers matching the diff's file types. OUT — named as deliberate exclusions, not omissions: issue investigation, the spec, domain/context docs, the planReview focus, and the plan-review contract file; the light packet is what keeps Codex inside its runtime budget, and domain conformance belongs to the other axis. Output shape: first line an axis verdict (Correctness: Clean | Findings + 1-2 sentences), then exactly Critical / Important / Minor, <=400 words, every finding with stable ID, live path:line evidence, confidence, unknowns; `None.` under empty sections. Disposition: NOT this skill's job for diff-review — the validated result returns unmodified to the calling controller with the reviewer identity (Codex | Claude fallback + failure class) for its ledger; the same one-time native fallback and never-retry rules apply. Naming the size pre-flight is correct here, not a deviation: measuring the range with `diff-scope` after the capability pre-flight and finding it at or under 20 product files means the packet is dispatched exactly as described above — six items, no coverage sentence, no file list. Failures: reusing the plan-review packet 'plus tweaks', letting the reviewer grade spec conformance, or dispositioning findings inside this skill.

evals.name: diff-review-oversized-range-scoped-packet
evals.prompt: sdd's final review is dispatching you for the correctness axis: operation diff-review over `aaa1111..bbb2222` in this worktree, a branch that changes 44 product files. **Plan-only: launch nothing.** Tell me: which pre-flights you run and in what order, with the exact command for any helper you call; what this packet contains that an under-budget packet would not, and what it no longer contains; how the reviewer is told to obtain the diff it reviews; what the reviewer's first line must look like; what you hand back to the calling controller; and what you do in each of these situations: (a) `diff-scope` is not installed on this machine; (b) Codex comes back `CODEX_REVIEW_FAILURE: job timed out` on this dispatch.
evals.expected_output: Pre-flights, in this order: first the shared capability pre-flight `command -v codex-companion`; then diff-review's own size pre-flight, run from the worktree root as `diff-scope <base>..<head> --root <absolute worktree root> --artifact-path <specDir> --artifact-path <planDir> --format json` (helper at `~/.agents/bin/diff-scope`; defaults `.claude/specs` / `.claude/plans` when the dispatcher has no bindings, never omitting the flags). Exactly three fields are read — `product.changed_files`, `files[].path`, `files[].changed_lines`; `product.changed_lines` and `excluded` are deliberately not read, they belong to the degradation gate. 44 > 20, so the packet is scoped to the first 20 entries of `files[]` taken verbatim — no filtering and no re-ranking, the helper's churn-descending, path-tie-broken order is already a total order, so the same range always yields the same 20 paths, and binary rows (churn zero) sort last so they never displace a text file. The scoped packet differs from the six-item packet in exactly three places: item 2 changes subject to the listed product files as changed across the range and gains a coverage sentence in substance — this is a scoped review, 20 of 44 changed product files, selected as the highest-churn files, files outside the list are not under review in this pass, do not treat their absence from the list as evidence they are clean, and every reported finding must be anchored in a listed file; item 4 retains the manifest root path and all four metrics as range-coverage evidence but says do not read its shards, because reading the full-range shards would defeat the scope — item 3's rubric receives every manifest/metric placeholder and routes on the explicit scoped statement; and a new item 7 lists the 20 paths, worktree-root-relative, one per line, in the helper's order, each with its changed-line count, as a collection instruction: fetch `git diff <base>..<head> -- ':(literal)<path>'` once per listed path and treat that set as the whole of the range under review, with the invocation protocol spelled out — one invocation per path, the path passed as a single literal argument after `--`, never shell-joined with the other listed paths into one command line, and pathspec magic disabled by the `:(literal)` prefix, because the helper emits whatever bytes Git records (spaces, newlines, non-UTF-8, a leading `:`). Nothing else changes; no per-file diffs are embedded, the packet stays a paths packet, and the conformance axis plus every unscoped reviewer reads the strict manifest and all shards once in manifest order, explicitly reporting unreadable evidence. Scoping bounds what is supplied and what is graded, not what may be consulted: the rubric's carve-out for one focused check per concrete named risk survives, so a cross-file finding reaching into an unlisted file is legal and reportable, provided the finding is anchored in a listed file — an unlisted file may be consulted and cited as evidence, but a defect lying wholly within an unlisted file is outside this pass and is not reported. First line: `**Correctness:** Clean — scoped to 20 of 44 product files; <assessment>` or `**Correctness:** Findings — scoped to 20 of 44 product files; <assessment>` — the coverage opens the em-dash assessment clause, never sitting between the verdict word and the dash (agent-evidence.py fullmatches that line), and a scoped review never uses the bare `**Correctness:** Clean` form. Hand-off: the validated three-section result unmodified, plus the reviewer identity and the scope `scoped: 20 of 44 product files`, for the calling controller's ledger — the controller records what it is given and never re-derives the measurement. Case (a): a missing, non-zero-exiting or unparsable helper is no measurement, never a failure — dispatch exactly as today (six items including item 4's manifest root path and all four metrics, today's verdict format) and report `unmeasured`; it never spends the one-time native fallback and never triggers a retry. Case (b): that IS a real Codex failure — exactly one fresh native reviewer gets the SAME scoped packet, item 7 and coverage sentence intact, the failure class is recorded, Codex is not retried. Failures: treating the oversized diff as a Codex failure or spending the one-time fallback on it; reading the manifest's full-range shards on a scoped dispatch — the reviewer's evidence then widens beyond the selected paths; omitting the manifest root or any metric; regenerating a pathspec-limited package; embedding per-file diffs; shell-joining the listed paths into a single `git diff` invocation or interpolating them without the `:(literal)` prefix; putting the coverage between `Clean` and the dash, or omitting it altogether on a scoped dispatch (nothing downstream catches that — `agent-evidence.py` never sees whether the packet was scoped); filtering binary rows or re-ranking the helper's output; reading `product.changed_lines` or `excluded` into the scoping decision; scoping a range that measures exactly 20 product files; measuring before the capability pre-flight.
